data.name: Gauresh
data.gender_notes: Gauresh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gau (cow) Rishi (seer) - One who takes care of cows, a revered figure in Hinduism, particularly associated with Lord Krishna. The name Gauresh carries the meaning “Cowherd lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gauresh usually hope their child will grow to embody cowherd lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that symbolizes devotion to Lord Krishna and the sacred duty of taking care of living beings.
data.etymology: Gauresh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Cowherd lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gauresh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Gauresh" is deeply rooted in the rich cultural tradition of India. The prefix "Gau" is derived from the revered symbol of the cow in Hinduism. Cows are considered sacred creatures in Indian culture and the protector of dharma. The Hanuman Chalisa, a famous Hindu devotional text, outrightly states, "Gau mataas poshak lochan virakta hathi huu nandan," which translates to "Gau Mata (Cow Mother) wears the reddish-colored bangles (on her arms) and the calf stands beside her, weeping."
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, the name 'Gauresh' resonates deeply with the devotees of Lord Krishna, who is known by many names like 'Gokul Nath' and 'Gau-mata-purush'--the protector and preserver of the cows. In Hindu mythology, Lord Krishna was raised in the Vrindavan forests, which was abundant in cows, as he was the eternal caretaker of the cows and their calves. This spiritual significance can be derived from a line in the Bhagavada Gita, the sacred Hindu text, where Krishna says "Dadamhi Sva-bhakitahkair Sustaarth-Anubhavah, Sarv-bhoota-Bhavaatma Bhavyo Bh Cohen Nityam Mam Pashyati." This means, "Those who see Me as the Mac-chela (Krishna's devotee) and love Me with devotion, I become theirs by making them reach the divine abode eventually."
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gauresh signifies the divine protector and guide of Gau or cows. His name is a reminder of the spiritual significance of respecting and nurturing all forms of life, particularly the noble bovine creature.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Gauresh was a king of the Satavahana dynasty in the 2nd century AD The name Gauresh carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Gauresh ruled over the region of Andhra Pradesh in India

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Hindu name websites where expectant parents research meaningful names. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
